sectorLine: Industrials — Motion control, transport equipment & accessibility
headlineHtml: The reducer cycle trough is behind it; the portfolio is smaller, purer — and the 2027 reference targets now rest on Transport and Accessibility
ledeLeadHtml: Nabtesco is Japan's motion-control specialist: the world's leading maker of precision reduction gears for industrial robots (Component Solutions), alongside railway, aircraft and marine control equipment (Transport Solutions) and automatic doors and platform systems (Accessibility Solutions).
ledeHtml: In FY12/2025 revenue was ¥307,912mn and operating profit ¥20,726mn (6.7% margin) on the continuing basis — the hydraulics business was classified as a discontinued operation from Q3 FY2025 and 70% of it was transferred to Comer Industries on 1 January 2026. FY12/2026 guidance, raised on 31 July 2026 and left unchanged at Q3 (13 November 2026), is revenue ¥344,000mn, operating profit ¥32,600mn, profit before tax ¥36,300mn and owners' net income ¥24,100mn (basic EPS ¥206.20, dividend ¥82). Strengths: (1) a structural franchise in RV precision reducers for industrial robots, where Nabtesco holds the leading global share and the FY2023–25 downturn was a customer inventory cycle, not share loss on any disclosed evidence; (2) Transport Solutions has compounded steadily — sales ¥67,744mn (FY2021) to ¥100,473mn (FY2025) at a 13.5% margin — on rail, aircraft and marine demand, and now carries ¥100,199mn of the ¥180,055mn group backlog; (3) Accessibility grows through cycles (¥75,108mn to ¥110,668mn over the same span) on platform-door and automatic-door demand; (4) order intake has exceeded ¥320bn for four consecutive years (FY2022–25) and the backlog is at a record; (5) the balance sheet is in net cash (cash ¥73,340mn vs borrowings ¥44,985mn at FY2025-end, register definition). Weaknesses: (1) profitability has structurally de-rated — group OP margin fell from 10.0% (FY2021) to 4.6% (FY2024) before recovering to 6.7%, and Component Solutions' profit collapsed from ¥22,903mn to ¥5,420mn as reducer demand and then the hydraulics exit shrank the segment from ¥138,130mn to ¥79,325mn of sales; (2) the FY2025/FY2026 comparison crosses the hydraulics discontinuation, so reported growth rates flatter or depress underlying trends depending on the line; (3) the mid-term plan's hard targets are financial-engineering metrics (ROIC ≥10%, DOE ≥3.5% by 2027) while the operating reference targets (2027 revenue ¥400bn, OP ¥42bn) were set in February 2025 — whether they include the transferred hydraulics profit is an open question the company has not answered in the sources read; (4) on 30 September 2026 the company filed amendments to internal control reports for prior fiscal years and disclosed material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting; (5) FY2021's headline profit is unusable as a base — a ¥117,221mn first-quarter financial gain, partly reversed over the rest of that year, took owners' net income to ¥64,818mn and diluted EPS to ¥534.53.

bullets.leadHtml: Guidance raised once, held at Q3
bullets.html: FY12/2026 guidance was set on 12 February 2026 (revenue ¥327,000mn / OP ¥27,700mn / owners' NI ¥17,600mn), the net-income line alone was raised in April (to ¥18,600mn — a step the guidance tracker flags as only partially verified), and the full guide was raised on 31 July 2026 to revenue ¥344,000mn / OP ¥32,600mn / PBT ¥36,300mn / NI ¥24,100mn; it was left unchanged at Q3 on 13 November 2026. At Q3 the company reported progress of 73% on revenue and 72% on OP, implying a Q4 of ¥93.2bn revenue and ¥9.2bn OP (calculated); management attributed the soft implied Q4 segment margins to Q4-weighted expenses and cost-recognition timing in the Q&A.

The hydraulics business was split off (as Comtesco) and 70% transferred to Comer Industries on 1 January 2026; it is a discontinued operation from Q3 FY2025 (post-tax result +¥1,901mn in FY2025). FY2025 is therefore continuing-only while FY2024 and earlier are on the combined basis — Component Solutions' reported fall from ¥110,571mn (FY2024) to ¥79,325mn (FY2025) is mostly scope, not demand.

Component Solutions earned ¥22,903mn on ¥138,130mn of sales in FY2021 (16.6% margin) and ¥5,420mn on ¥79,325mn in FY2025 (6.8%) — reducer destocking plus the hydraulics exit. Transport Solutions moved the other way every year: ¥67,744mn → ¥100,473mn of sales and ¥5,617mn → ¥13,586mn of profit (FY2021–25), and holds 56% of the group order backlog.

bullets.leadHtml: Mid-term plan: hard targets are ratios
bullets.html: The 2025–2027 plan 'Reviving Potential, Evolving Excellence' (February 2025, company plan) sets hard targets of ROIC ≥10% and DOE ≥3.5% by 2027, with reference targets of revenue ¥400bn, OP ¥42bn and a 10.5% OP margin. The FY2026 guide (OP ¥32,600mn) leaves ¥9.4bn of OP to find in the plan's final year; 'Project 10' is the profitability-repair programme beneath it, and management says its price-increase target has been achieved while material-cost inflation ran above plan.

On 30 September 2026 Nabtesco announced amendments to its internal control reports for prior fiscal years and the identification of material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, discovered during the Q2 FY2026 accounting process (company release). The Q3 results were published on schedule on 13 November 2026 and guidance was unchanged; the remediation status is a monitoring item for this coverage.

blocks.heading: 1. Key indicators and financial history
blocks.html:
Exhibit 1 (page 1) summarises ten fiscal years, FY12/2016–FY12/2025. FY2016 is J-GAAP as originally filed (Nabtesco adopted IFRS from FY2017); FY2017–FY2024 are IFRS on the combined basis (hydraulics inside Component Solutions); FY2025 is IFRS continuing operations only, hydraulics being a discontinued operation from Q3 FY2025 (register S7, S14–S15). The bases are never spliced in this report.

Three eras are visible. First, steady scale on thin margins: sales rose from ¥244,618mn (FY2016) to ¥294,626mn (FY2018), with OP between ¥21,889mn and ¥29,468mn (7.4–10.4%). Second, the FY2021 distortion: sales of ¥299,802mn and OP of ¥30,017mn were ordinary, but financial income of +¥69,850mn net for the year — a +¥117,221mn first quarter partly reversed by −¥47,371mn over Q2–Q4 (register S13) — lifted PBT to ¥101,966mn, owners' net income to ¥64,818mn and diluted EPS to ¥534.53; none of the FY2021 below-OP lines is a usable base. Third, the reducer downturn and portfolio surgery: sales peaked at ¥333,631mn in FY2023 while OP slid for three straight years to ¥14,788mn (4.6%) in FY2024 as reducer destocking, China weakness and cost inflation compounded; FY2025's continuing OP recovered to ¥20,726mn (6.7%).

Cash generation held up better than profit: operating cash flow was positive in all ten years (¥7,717mn at the FY2022 low; ¥32,824mn in FY2025). Order intake has run at ¥286–335bn a year and the backlog has built every year since FY2020, from ¥130,944mn to ¥180,055mn. Capital expenditure peaked at ¥28,351mn in FY2024 (capacity additions ahead of the cycle) and fell back to ¥16,015mn in FY2025. R&D and headcount are disclosed in the annual supplement only: R&D was ¥7,362mn and employees 7,162 in FY2016, rising to ¥10,214mn and 7,713 by FY2018 (history block); the FY2021–25 supplement values were not carried into the sheet's main block and are marked as a gap.

blocks.heading: 2. Latest update — Q3 FY12/2026 results and the FY12/2026 guidance chain
blocks.html: FY2025 results (12 February 2026) and the Q3 FY2026 tanshin (13 November 2026) frame the current year; segment detail is in Chapter 5 and the full chain is in Exhibit 3.

blocks.heading: Q3 FY12/2026 progress
blocks.html: At Q3 FY2026 the company reported cumulative progress of 73% of the full-year revenue guide and 72% of the OP guide (company presentation), implying Q4 revenue of ¥93.2bn and OP of ¥9.2bn (calculated from the guide). In the Q&A the company explained the soft implied Q4 margins at segment level by Q4-weighted expenses and delayed cost recognition — ¥0.2bn landing in Q3 and ¥0.4bn in Q4 in CMP (Component Solutions), and a ¥0.5bn cost delay in TRS (Transport Solutions) also landing in Q4 (company Q&A, 13 November 2026). The share price fell 13.9% on the next trading day (16 November 2026 close ¥3,574) — the market is pricing the Q4 cost load and the internal-control disclosure (Chapter 8) rather than the unchanged full-year guide. The only revised segment guidance figure verified in the sources read is CMP operating profit, raised from ¥7,000mn to ¥9,700mn on 31 July 2026; the full revised segment guidance table is 未取得.

blocks.heading: Guidance chain (Exhibit 3)
blocks.html: Initial guidance (12 February 2026, with the FY2025 tanshin): revenue ¥327,000mn, OP ¥27,700mn, owners' NI ¥17,600mn. Revision 1 (30 April 2026, Q1): revenue and OP unchanged, owners' NI raised to ¥18,600mn — the guidance tracker flags this step as only partially verified: it rests on the TDnet XBRL forecast history, and the net-income basis (continuing vs total including discontinued hydraulics) differs between sources. Revision 2 (31 July 2026, Q2 tanshin): revenue ¥344,000mn, OP ¥32,600mn, PBT ¥36,300mn, owners' NI ¥24,100mn, basic EPS ¥206.20, dividend ¥82 (¥41 interim + ¥41 year-end). Q3 (13 November 2026): unchanged. Against FY2025 continuing actuals, the guide implies revenue +11.7%, OP +57.3% and owners' NI +53.5% (calculated) — a steep second-half-weighted recovery that leans on reducer demand normalisation and the Transport/Accessibility backlog.

blocks.heading: 3. Business description
blocks.html:
Nabtesco was formed in 2003 from the merger of Teijin Seiki and Nabco. It reports three segments plus an 'Other' category, organised as internal companies: the Component Solutions segment (precision reduction gears — the RV reducer line for industrial-robot joints and machine tools — and, until the 2026 transfer, hydraulics), Transport Solutions (railway vehicle equipment, aircraft flight-control components, marine control systems, and automotive components), Accessibility Solutions (automatic doors, platform screen doors, welfare equipment) and Other (packaging machinery, 3D modelling equipment and similar). Headquarters are in Hirakawa-cho, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo. Representative Director, President & CEO is Kazumasa Kimura (in the role since 2023; Katsuhiro Teramoto is Chairman).

Capacity, not demand, is the disclosed constraint in the reducer franchise. The company puts precision-reducer capacity at 1.15 million units a year across the Tsu and Changzhou plants and the ramping Hamamatsu plant; in Q3 FY12/2026 utilisation was 85% at Tsu and 95% at Changzhou, with Hamamatsu output expanding gradually and its further expansion timing to be judged against demand because Tsu still has headroom. Reducer orders in Q3 were flat quarter on quarter but up 18% year on year, at what management called a past-peak level; it attributes the strength not to broad automotive capex, which it calls not strong, but to competition among Chinese automakers and to higher reducer unit prices. North American automotive robot demand, almost none last year on the company's account, is gradually starting to move in 2026 and is expected to contribute from FY12/2027.

blocks.heading: Component Solutions — the reducer franchise, minus hydraulics
blocks.html: The RV precision reducer is the group's crown jewel: a cycloidal reduction gear used in the joints of articulated industrial robots, where Nabtesco holds the leading global share (company materials; the exact share is not disclosed in the tanshin set). The segment also includes precision gears for machine tools. Until 31 December 2025 it included the hydraulics business (travel motors and valves for construction machinery), which was split into Comtesco and 70%-transferred to Comer Industries on 1 January 2026; Nabtesco retains 30% and an equity-method interest. On the combined basis the segment's sales fell from ¥138,130mn (FY2021) to ¥110,571mn (FY2024) through the robot-capex downturn, and on the continuing basis were ¥79,325mn in FY2025 — the drop from FY2024 is mostly the hydraulics scope removal. Segment profit fell from ¥22,903mn (16.6%) to ¥5,420mn (6.8%). Capacity questions are live: the interview pack records utilisation of 85% at the Tsu plant and 95% at Changzhou, with an expansion deferred — whether that is discipline or under-investment into the next upcycle (including any humanoid ramp) is the segment's central debate.

blocks.heading: Transport Solutions — the compounding second engine
blocks.html: Railway equipment (brake systems, door operators), aircraft components (flight-control actuation — Nabtesco is a long-standing Boeing supplier), marine control systems and automotive parts. Sales grew every year from ¥67,744mn (FY2021) to ¥100,473mn (FY2025), profit from ¥5,617mn (8.3%) to ¥13,586mn (13.5%), and the order backlog reached ¥100,199mn — 56% of the group total — giving the segment multi-year visibility unusual in the group. Order intake of ¥109,354mn in FY2025 exceeded sales, so the backlog is still building.

blocks.heading: Accessibility Solutions — doors and platforms
blocks.html: Automatic doors for buildings, platform screen doors for rail stations, and welfare/accessibility equipment. Sales rose from ¥75,108mn (FY2021) to ¥110,668mn (FY2025); profit recovered from a ¥2,830mn trough (FY2022, 3.6% margin) to ¥9,085mn (8.2%). The business is project-based — backlog ¥47,803mn — and less cyclical than Component, but margin has never sustainably exceeded ~10% in the window.

blocks.heading: Other
blocks.html: Packaging machinery, 3D modelling equipment and other non-reportable businesses: sales ¥17,445mn and profit ¥2,194mn in FY2025 (FY2021: ¥18,820mn / ¥2,736mn) — a stable, sub-scale tail that the portfolio review has so far left untouched.

blocks.heading: 4. Market and value chain
blocks.html: Component Solutions sells into industrial-robot and machine-tool capex: the reducer cycle follows robot orders (JARA/IFR data) with a lag, and the FY2023–25 downturn was a post-COVID inventory correction in robots layered on weak China demand. Competition in precision reducers is concentrated — Harmonic Drive Systems in harmonic gears, Nabtesco in RV reducers — with Chinese makers (e.g. Transport demand is driven by rail fleet renewal and platform-door installation in Japan and Asia, aircraft build rates (Boeing/Airbus supply chains) and marine newbuild cycles. Accessibility demand follows construction and station-modernisation spending. Cost side: steel and materials inflation ran ahead of the company's initial assumptions in the current plan period (company Q&A), partly offset by the price increases management says are now achieved.

blocks.heading: 5. Segments and regions
blocks.html:
Segment profit is operating profit on the company's definition (register, Drivers). FY2025 is continuing-only; FY2024 and earlier include hydraulics inside Component Solutions — the two bases are shown in one table with the break flagged, never spliced into a growth rate.

The regional history tempers the China narrative. Japan was 55.5% of sales in FY2017 (¥156,800mn of ¥282,422mn) and 50.4% in FY2025 (¥155,240mn of ¥307,912mn) — Japanese sales were essentially flat in yen across eight years while the group grew. China sales peaked in the window at ¥59,510mn in FY2021 and fell to ¥43,403mn by FY2025, a 27% decline from the peak, even as reducer orders from Chinese automakers drove the FY12/2026 recovery described in Chapter 2. Europe was the growth region of the main window, rising from ¥42,259mn in FY2021 to ¥59,671mn in FY2025, and North America rose from ¥16,623mn to ¥27,490mn over the same span. Regional profit is not disclosed in any year.

blocks.heading: Segments (Exhibit 2)
blocks.html: FY2025 vs FY2021 tells the portfolio story. Component: sales ¥138,130mn → ¥79,325mn, profit ¥22,903mn → ¥5,420mn (the FY2024 combined-basis staging point was ¥110,571mn / ¥4,523mn — the margin trough preceded the scope change). Transport: ¥67,744mn → ¥100,473mn, profit ¥5,617mn → ¥13,586mn. Accessibility: ¥75,108mn → ¥110,668mn, profit ¥7,642mn → ¥9,085mn. Other: ¥18,820mn → ¥17,445mn, profit ¥2,736mn → ¥2,194mn. Corporate/eliminations ran at −¥9,559mn in FY2025 (−¥8,881mn in FY2021; the FY2023–24 prints of −¥10,380mn and −¥12,283mn include the downturn years' unallocated costs). In the deepened years the solution basis exists from FY2017 (Component ¥119,280mn / ¥20,197mn profit in FY2018; Transport ¥81,863mn / ¥2,007mn; Accessibility ¥75,957mn / ¥4,625mn); FY2016 is on the OLD four-segment basis only (Precision Equipment ¥56,931mn / ¥8,616mn; Transport Equipment ¥61,074mn / ¥10,335mn; Aircraft & Hydraulic Equipment ¥47,806mn / −¥26mn; Industrial Equipment ¥78,806mn / ¥4,546mn — profit sums directly to J-GAAP OP), taken from the FY2016 tanshin's own segment note, not the FY2017 restatement.

blocks.heading: Regions
blocks.html: Regional sales are by customer location, six disclosed regions (register S4). FY2025: Japan ¥155,240mn (50.4% of sales), Europe ¥59,671mn (19.4%), China ¥43,403mn (14.1%), North America ¥27,490mn (8.9%), Asia ex-China ¥18,891mn (6.1%), Other ¥3,217mn (1.0%). The mix has internationalised slowly: Japan was 54.3% in FY2021 and China has shrunk from ¥59,510mn (19.9%, FY2021) to ¥43,403mn on the reducer downturn. In the history block the six-region basis runs from FY2017 (Japan ¥156,800mn; China ¥40,273mn; Europe ¥45,785mn); FY2016 has no regional disclosure (ND). Regional profit is not disclosed in any year.

blocks.heading: 6. Financial statements summary
blocks.html:
FY2025 (continuing): sales ¥307,912mn, gross profit ¥93,781mn (30.5% — the best margin of the window, flattered by the hydraulics scope removal and mix), SG&A ¥71,964mn (23.4% of sales), OP ¥20,726mn. Below OP: share of profit of associates ¥1,043mn and the discontinued hydraulics post-tax result +¥1,901mn give PBT of ¥23,557mn on the sheet's presentation (continuing PBT plus the post-tax discontinued result; register S7); total net income ¥17,625mn, owners' ¥15,695mn, diluted EPS ¥131.56 (sheet; Finnhub basic ¥131.554). Operating cash flow ¥32,824mn against capex of ¥16,015mn (CF basis). Balance sheet at FY2025-end: cash ¥73,340mn, borrowings ¥44,985mn (register S6 definition, leases excluded) — net cash ¥28,355mn (calculated); receivables ¥76,945mn, inventories ¥52,838mn (3.15 months of cost of sales, calculated), payables ¥52,009mn. FY2021's statement is the outlier documented in Chapter 1 (PBT ¥101,966mn on the financial gain). Total assets, equity and ROE are not carried in the sheet's main block and are marked as gaps rather than sourced elsewhere.

The FY2021 distortion can be sized exactly from the sheet's bridge. Financing income net was +¥69,850mn in FY2021, against -¥5,121mn in FY2022, +¥4,112mn in FY2023, +¥222mn in FY2024 and -¥113mn in FY2025 — the single line explains why FY2021 profit before tax of ¥101,966mn is 6.5 times the FY2022 figure of ¥15,763mn while operating profit fell only from ¥30,017mn to ¥18,097mn. The same history puts the FY2025 gross margin of 30.5% in context: the ten-year range is 26.2% (FY2020) to 30.5% (FY2025), with FY2016's 28.3% on the J-GAAP basis the only other year above 28% — the FY2025 margin step is therefore partly mix and scope (hydraulics removed) rather than a level the series has held before.

blocks.heading: 7. Strategy and mid-term plan
blocks.html: The mid-term plan 2025–2027, 'Reviving Potential, Evolving Excellence' (announced February 2025, company plan), sets hard targets of ROIC ≥10% and DOE ≥3.5% by 2027, a CO2 reduction of −50% by 2027 (2015 base), and reference (参考) targets for 2027 of revenue ¥400bn, OP ¥42bn and a 10.5% OP margin. 'Project 10' is the profitability-repair programme underneath; at the Q3 FY2026 briefing the company said its price-increase target has been achieved but material-cost increases came in larger than initially assumed. Two monitoring points: (i) the 2027 reference OP of ¥42bn versus the FY2026 guide of ¥32,600mn implies a +29% final-year step (calculated), before asking whether the reference figures — set in February 2025, before the hydraulics transfer closed — include the disposed business's profit; the interview pack records this as an open question to management; (ii) the hard targets being ratios (ROIC/DOE) rather than absolute profit makes delivery partly a capital-policy question — buybacks and DOE management count toward them. Portfolio direction is toward purification (hydraulics out; CMP focused on precision reducers), with the retained 30% Comtesco stake keeping an equity-method link to Comer Industries.

blocks.heading: 8. Other information
blocks.html: Internal control: on 30 September 2026 the company announced that it had filed amendments to its internal control reports for prior fiscal years and identified material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, discovered in the course of the Q2 FY2026 accounting procedures (company news release, 30 September 2026). No restatement of headline results accompanied the Q3 publication in the sources read; remediation progress is a standing monitoring item. Shareholder returns: the FY2026 dividend guide is ¥82 per share (¥41 + ¥41); FY2025's dividend was ¥80 on the same split pattern (secondary source). Major shareholders are 未取得 in the sources used for this report. Employees were 7,717 at FY2020-end (annual supplement); a company-profile figure of 8,472 employees as of November 2026 appears in secondary databases (flagged as secondary, scope unverified). Next scheduled results: FY2026 full-year, February 2027 (11 February 2027 per secondary calendars).

blocks.heading: 9. Basis of preparation
blocks.html: Sources: the PL/segment sheet for Nabtesco (6268) — main window FY2021–FY2025 plus the FY2016–FY2020 history block, built from the annual and quarterly tanshin [IFRS] (FY2016 J-GAAP) with register S1–S17 — the guidance tracker (56-company edition, 17 November 2026), the interview pack for 6268, and company releases (mid-term plan, February 2025; internal-control notice, 30 September 2026). FY2025 figures are continuing operations; FY2024 comparatives are as originally reported on the combined basis (the FY2025 tanshin's continuing-only restatement of FY2024 was not used, per register S7). Segment profit is operating profit on the company's definition; regional sales are by customer location with 'Other regions' carried in the adjustment row of the sheet so the six disclosed regions tie to consolidated sales. The sheet's template 'Estimate' columns (mechanical extrapolations) were not used. Calculated figures are labelled as such. Gaps (未取得 / not disclosed): the full revised segment-by-segment guidance table for FY2026 (only the CMP OP figure is verified); R&D and employee counts for FY2021–25 in the sheet's main block (annual supplement (2) only; history-block values used for FY2016–20); production/sales units, capacity and utilisation (Tsu 85% / Changzhou 95% appear in the interview pack from company briefings, not the tanshin); regional profit (all years); FY2016 regional sales; total assets, equity and ROE from the sheet; the April 2026 guidance step's net-income basis (tracker: partially verified); whether the 2027 reference targets include hydraulics profit; major shareholders. The share price is the 16 November 2026 close (StockAnalysis / StockInvest); market capitalisation is StockAnalysis's figure for the same date.
